checkboxes.description: All interactive elements minimum 44px for touch (buttons, links, icons)

evidence.reasoning: Most buttons have adequate touch targets (44px+) like form buttons (px-4 py-2), user avatar (w-12 h-12 = 48px), and hamburger menu (p-2 + icon = ~36px). However, several interactive elements fall short: MoreHorizontal action buttons use p-1 with size={16} (~32px), pagination arrow buttons use px-3 py-1 (~32-36px), and table action cells use p-1 rounded-full (~32px). These are below the 44px minimum touch target guideline.

checkboxes.description: Scroll performance smooth on lists/tables without lag

evidence.reasoning: Basic scroll implementation exists with overflow-x-auto for tables and overflow-y-auto for modals. However, no performance optimizations are implemented: no virtual scrolling for long lists, no scroll throttling/debouncing, no will-change CSS properties, and no lazy loading. The table uses min-w-[640px] which forces horizontal scroll on mobile but provides no smooth scroll behavior optimization. For small datasets this may work, but performance could degrade with larger lists.

checkboxes.description: Forms optimized for mobile (appropriate input types, sizes)

evidence.reasoning: Forms use appropriate input type='number' for numeric fields (monthly_cost), which triggers numeric keyboard on mobile. However, missing mobile-optimized input types: no type='url' for website_url/icon_url fields (uses generic text input), no type='email' if email fields exist, no type='tel' for phone numbers. Form layout uses grid-cols-2 which may be cramped on small mobile screens without responsive adjustment to single column.
evidence.snippet:

  <Field label="Coût mensuel (€) *" error={field.state.meta.errors?.[0]?.message}>
    <input type="number" className={inputClass} value={field.state.value} onChange={e => field.handleChange(Number(e.target.value))} />
  </Field>
)} />

evidence.reasoning: URL input fields use generic text type instead of type='url', missing mobile keyboard optimization that would provide URL-specific keyboard with .com and / shortcuts on mobile devices.

checkboxes.description: Swipe gestures implemented if applicable (drawer, carousel) - optional feature

evidence.reasoning: No swipe gesture implementation found in the codebase. No touch event handlers (onTouchStart, onTouchMove, onTouchEnd), no swipe gesture libraries (react-swipeable, framer-motion gestures), no carousel or drawer components that would benefit from swipe interactions. The mobile menu uses click/tap only, and there are no swipeable cards or galleries. This is an optional feature and its absence is acceptable.

reasoning: Mobile UX evaluation reveals partial implementation of mobile-friendly patterns. The hamburger menu is fully functional with proper state management and navigation callbacks (3/3 points). Touch targets are mostly adequate for primary actions but several secondary interactive elements (action dropdowns, pagination buttons) fall below the 44px guideline (2/4 points). Scroll performance uses basic CSS overflow properties without optimization techniques like virtual scrolling or momentum scrolling (1/2 points). Forms use type='number' appropriately but miss type='url' for URL fields and use non-responsive grid-cols-2 layout (1/2 points). No swipe gestures are implemented, which is acceptable as an optional feature (0/1 points). Total: 7/12 points (58%). The application demonstrates mobile awareness with responsive breakpoints and hamburger navigation, but lacks polish in touch target sizing, input type optimization, and performance enhancements for smooth mobile scrolling.
